name: VSCodium
tagline: VS Code without Microsoft's build, branding or telemetry
description: Community-built binaries of the open-source code that VS Code is made from. It is the same editor, with telemetry disabled and the vendor-neutral Open VSX registry in place of Microsoft's Marketplace.
backing: Community volunteers, building from Microsoft's MIT-licensed source

maturity.rationale: It is VS Code: the same codebase, rebuilt by a community project that has tracked upstream releases since 2018.

strengths: The identical editor: same interface, settings format, keybindings and extension API
Telemetry disabled and no Microsoft account prompts
Your settings.json, keybindings and most extensions carry straight over
Uses the vendor-neutral Open VSX extension registry
weaknesses: Microsoft's proprietary extensions are not licensed for it: Pylance, C# Dev Kit, the Remote Development pack and Live Share are unavailable or do not work
Open VSX has fewer extensions than Microsoft's Marketplace, and some lag behind
Settings Sync through a Microsoft or GitHub account is not available
Still downstream of Microsoft: the roadmap is theirs

featureNotes.vscode-extensions: From Open VSX; Microsoft-proprietary extensions excluded
featureNotes.remote-dev: Through community remote extensions rather than Microsoft's
